channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: N.Y. Sen. Gillibrand says new allegations in Cornell case are 'serious and horrific'
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with New York Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand about the reopening of the rape case at Cornell University, and her history of pushing legislation to curb campus sexual assault.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Juana Summers talks with New York Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand about the reopening of the rape case at Cornell University, and her history of pushing legislation to curb campus sexual assault.
item.dc:creator: Juana Summers

item.title: FBI says it's addressing massive data breach, vows to go after hackers
item.description: The FBI says it's aggressively investigating a massive data breach. But some FBI personnel are still trying to get answers to how much sensitive information was compromised.
item.content:encoded: The FBI says it's aggressively investigating a massive data breach. But some FBI personnel are still trying to get answers to how much sensitive information was compromised.
item.dc:creator: Jenna McLaughlin

item.title: This startup wants to prove gene-editing embryos is safe for making healthy babies
item.description: Origin Genomics aims to prove that the potential benefits of its technology for editing disease-causing genes in human embryos outweigh the risks.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: This year's MacArthur Fellows include researchers who fuse science and justice
item.description: The MacArthur Foundation has just announced its latest batch of 20 fellows. Among the recipients of the $800,000 "no-strings-attached" fellowships are researchers who were recognized for their work at the intersection of science and justice.

item.title: Could a far left candidate win a midterm race in a red state like Florida?
item.description: Angie Nixon, the Democratic U.S. Senate Candidate in Florida, is running from the far left — raising questions about whether such a campaign can work in a red state like Florida.
item.content:encoded: Angie Nixon, the Democratic U.S. Senate Candidate in Florida, is running from the far left — raising questions about whether such a campaign can work in a red state like Florida.

item.title: In 'Sophie, Standing There,' a fictional sound tech mics up (real) famous authors
item.description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly talks with writer Meg Mason about her latest book, Sophie, Standing There, and the one-sided relationships we form with some of our favorite authors.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly talks with writer Meg Mason about her latest book, Sophie, Standing There, and the one-sided relationships we form with some of our favorite authors.

item.title: Tennessee's failed execution ignites a medical ethics debate
item.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, ever. No matter the method.
item.content:encoded: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, ever. No matter the method.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Sweeney

item.title: AI has sparked anxiety, earlier generations showed us ways to manage our fears
item.description: Much of what we are hearing about AI leaves many people anxious about the risks posed by the technology. The writer Michael Sacacas takes a long view of how to manage such feelings.

item.title: Chatbots are becoming a new reality for renters
item.description: Landlords are using AI chatbots to manage interactions with their tenants. We hear from one renter who just wants help from a human.

item.title: The poverty rate among older Americans is rising, survey shows
item.description: Bucking the national trend, poverty has been steadily rising among seniors and older adults. A new survey sheds light on how low-income people are struggling in the crucial years before retirement.
